transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m having a hard time keeping my focus at work. I’ll be trying to finish an estimate or fill out a code form, and then a tool noise, or a text, or just some new idea about the workshop pulls me away. Then I come back and I’ve mixed up parts of different jobs. It’s starting to cause problems.
Did you have this same kind of trouble paying attention when you were a child?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember it being a big issue when I was a kid, but I wasn’t paying attention to it like that either. I got through school okay, from what I remember.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot?
I mean, I worry about work stuff when I mess something up or I’m behind, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying all the time. It’s more that I get distracted and then stress about the consequences.
Have you been feeling down or depressed বেশিরভাগ days lately?
I’m not sure I’d call it depressed most days. I’ve been frustrated and stressed because of the work mistakes, but I haven’t really noticed feeling down all the time.
Before age 12, did you often have trouble staying focused?
I honestly don’t know. I don’t really remember having a big problem staying focused before I was 12, but it’s kind of hard to say looking back.
Do you drink alcohol?
I’m not sure what to say exactly. I don’t really have anything specific to report about that.
Have your focus problems ever happened after drinking alcohol?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern of my focus getting worse after drinking.
Did your trouble focusing start after a specific stressful event?

Yeah, I think so. It’s been building for about seven months, around when we took on the mortgage for the workshop and the equipment. That stress kind of started it, or at least that’s when I really noticed it.
Outside of work, do you also have the same trouble staying focused?

Yeah, outside of work too, but it shows up the most when I’m trying to do paperwork or estimates. I’ll start on one thing, then a text comes in or I hear a tool noise or I get some new idea about the workshop, and I’m off on that instead. Then I come back and realize I’ve mixed up parts of jobs or lost where I was.
Aside from when there’s a clear work problem, do you find yourself feeling anxious most days?
I don’t know that I’d say most days. I mean, I get anxious when there’s something going wrong at work or money stuff comes up, but outside of that I haven’t really noticed it being constant.
Do you remember your school report cards ever saying you were easily distracted or had trouble paying attention?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember my report cards saying that, and I haven’t looked at them in years. I don’t think it was ever a big thing that got brought up to me.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought of it that way. I still do the things I usually like when I get the chance, so I don’t know that I’d say I’ve lost interest.
Since the workshop mortgage stress started, have unwanted thoughts about it been popping into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

I’m not sure I’d call them unwanted thoughts exactly. I do think about the mortgage stuff when something reminds me of it, or when I’m trying to plan things, but I haven’t really noticed it just popping into my head all the time on its own.
Since the workshop financial stress started, have you been feeling constantly on edge?
I don’t know if I’d say constantly. I’ve been stressed about it, yeah, but I haven’t really noticed feeling on edge all the time.
Have these focus problems caused clear problems for you at home?

Yeah. At home it’s been causing problems. My wife and I keep getting into arguments about the mortgage and the business, and she feels like I’m risking everything we built. It’s not just work stuff staying at work anymore.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic or revved up?

Yeah, there have been times like that. I’ve been kind of going nonstop — from job sites to putting in bids, then back in the workshop rewiring test panels. I’ll start some new home-automation idea before I’ve even finished the last one. It’s like sitting still feels like I’m wasting time.
During those revved-up times, do you need less sleep than usual?

Yeah. For months now I’ve been sleeping maybe three or four hours, and then I’m up before dawn like I’m ready to go. I’ll start pricing materials, answering emails, sketching out another system… and I don’t really feel tired like I should.
During those times when you’re sleeping only a few hours and still feel energized, have you felt unusually confident or believed you could do things other people would say are unrealistic?

Yeah… I have. I keep thinking I can just jump into bigger commercial jobs and train a whole crew right now, like I’m ready to scale everything up. And part of me knows I’m not fully licensed or experienced for some of that yet, but in those moments it feels like I can handle it.
During these energized periods, have you done things that were risky or caused problems for you?

Yeah… it has started causing problems. Clients have been complaining that I’m missing details or mixing up schedules, and my apprentices don’t really trust my direction like they used to.

And at home, it’s been bad. My wife and I keep arguing about the mortgage and the business. She feels like I’m risking everything we built, and… I can see why she’d think that.
What is the longest time these revved-up periods have lasted without letting up?
Probably about seven months now. It started building around when we took on the mortgage for the workshop and equipment, and it hasn’t really let up since then.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a bipolar-spectrum mood episode with sustained decreased need for sleep, increased energy/activity, grandiose/unrealistic confidence, distractibility, goal-directed overactivity, and resulting occupational and marital impairment. Although symptoms emerged in the context of financial stress, the syndrome is more consistent with bipolar disorder than ADHD, anxiety, or a stress-related disorder. ADHD is weakened by lack of clear childhood onset, and anxiety/stress disorders are weakened by absence of pervasive worry, intrusive stress symptoms, or constant hyperarousal.
